input.brief: Daily Slip turns everyday spending into a daily printed receipt, tactile printer and memory shelf

direction.name: The page is the object
direction.idea: Find the printed or physical artefact that already exists in the subject's world and build the page as that thing. A wedding site is the invitation card. A restaurant is its menu. A conference is the ticket; a record is its sleeve; a shop is the receipt or the swing tag; an archive is a stack of tabbed folders; a course is the syllabus sheet. The artefact supplies everything a template would otherwise invent: its proportions, its typographic manners, its way of grouping information. Visitors recognise the object instantly, which is why these pages feel specific.
direction.composition: The first screen shows the artefact as a single filled panel (paper colour on a contrasting ground) centred or offset, with believable proportions: a card at 5:7, a ticket at about 2.2:1 with a notch cut by `clip-path`, a menu as a tall sheet. All primary content lives on it, set the way that object is set: centred and symmetrical for an invitation, in tidy aligned columns for a menu or ticket. The ground behind is a flat colour or one full-bleed photograph. As the page continues, each section is another piece of the same stationery: a second card, a tear-off stub, a folded panel, always filled shapes with real edges (straight, notched, scalloped, perforated by a dotted `border` of round dots at 4px or more), never outlined boxes. The footer is the back of the object.
direction.typography: Take the manners of the artefact: a bookish serif with small caps avoided, or a blunt condensed face for tickets and posters. Sizes stay within what print would use relative to the panel; the name is large on the panel, details are small and exact.
direction.colour: Paper and ink plus the ground the paper sits on. Two or three flat colours in total, like a two-colour print job.
direction.imagery: Optional. One photograph behind the object, or small photographs placed on it like tipped-in plates. The object itself is the image.
direction.richness: Recognition. The shaped edges, the print-like alignment and the limited inks make a familiar object out of plain HTML.
direction.pitfalls: Choose an artefact that truly belongs to the subject, or it becomes costume. Shape the edges with fills and `clip-path`; an outlined rectangle with a thin border is not an object. Keep text sizes readable on a phone, where the object becomes full width with its shaped edge kept at top and bottom.

hero.name: Tabbed folder stack
hero.blueprint: A dark flat ground. A slim top row at 24px holds the wordmark dead centre and one text link far right at 15px. The headline is one centred line of heavy condensed capitals at clamp(96px, 10vw, 160px), spanning about 70% of the width, its cap line 110px from the top. Under it one supporting sentence in a serif at 20px, centred, max 46ch. From 51% of the height down the screen is a stack of five file folders: flat colour bands 86% of the viewport wide, centred, each offset 64px below the one behind so only a strip of the back four shows. Every folder has one trapezoid tab rising 40px from its top edge, cut with `clip-path: polygon()`, at its own horizontal position and in its own colour, holding one section name at 18px. The front folder is open and runs off the bottom edge; it carries the single action as a solid button at its top-left with 32px padding. Each folder links to its section and lends that section its ground colour. The tab shape returns as the button's top corners.
hero.mobile: The headline sits 96px down at 17vw on one line, or two at 15vw, centred, with the supporting sentence at 16px beneath. The folder stack starts at 48svh at full width: bands offset 52px, tabs 32px tall with names at 15px, staggered left, centre and right. The front folder runs off the bottom with the action button at full width inside it.
hero.headline: The name or a two-word statement on one line of up to about 12 characters at 10vw; two lines allowed on a phone.

motion.name: Index with preview
motion.description: Rows of text are the navigation through the work; pointing at a row brings up its image in one fixed frame and dims the other rows. On touch screens each row shows its image inline instead. Fast and exact (about 240ms crossfade), no lag behind the pointer. Recipe: 'List with image preview' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Title, note, facts row
sections.blueprint: First row: a heading of two to four words in a light weight at clamp(44px, 5vw, 76px) sits on the left margin in columns 1–6; a three-line paragraph at 16px, 260px wide, sits in columns 10–12 with its last line on the heading's baseline. Columns 7–9 stay empty. 120px lower, a second row sets three or four facts (a date, a time, a place, a price) as large light text at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px), spread across the 12 columns with `justify-content: space-between`. Each fact has a one-line explanation at 14px directly under it in the soft ink, left-aligned to the fact. Facts are separated only by the space between them, so the row reads like the line of times on a printed programme. A photograph may start under the right half of the facts row, 5 columns wide at 4:3. Padding 140px top, 120px bottom.
sections.mobile: Heading at 11vw on the left margin; the note follows directly under it at 16px, full width. The facts become a two-column grid with a 32px row gap, each fact at 26px with its explanation beneath. Any photograph goes last, full width.

sections.name: Itinerary on a slip
sections.blueprint: The process is printed as an itinerary or receipt. One paper-coloured slip 420–480px wide stands on a contrasting flat ground at columns 7–11; its bottom edge is a zigzag cut with clip-path and its top edge is straight. The heading, two to four words at clamp(40px, 4.4vw, 68px), sits in columns 1–5 with a 30ch paragraph, top-aligned with the slip. On the slip, in the text face at 16px with tabular figures: stages grouped under time headings that carry the order ('Monday', 'Midweek', 'Friday'), each heading in bold with 28px above it. Under a heading, two to four rows; each row has what happens on the left, a duration or time on the right, and a leader of round 4px dots between. The final row is inverted, paper-coloured text on a full-width ink bar 44px tall, and states the result: what the reader holds at the end and the total time.
sections.mobile: The heading and paragraph come first. The slip follows at full width minus 16px margins, keeping its zigzag bottom edge. Rows keep left text, dots and right value on one line; long descriptions wrap under the left text. The inverted final row stays full width.

sections.name: Photo tiles with label strips
sections.blueprint: Four columns with 12px gaps; every tile is a photograph with a filled label strip attached directly beneath it, the two forming one object like a print with its swing tag. The photograph is 1:1 or 4:5 with square corners. The strip is the same width, 84–96px tall with 12px padding, and holds two or three rows of text at 12–13px in the text face with tabular figures: row one spreads four short values evenly across the width with `justify-content: space-between`; row two puts a date at the left end and a time or place at the right end; row three names the maker or model. Strip and text colours change per tile through four palette pairs (dark on bright, bright on dark), so a uniform grid looks varied. Rows of tiles are 28px apart. A two- or three-word heading at 32px sits top-left, 40px above the grid. Holds 8–16 tiles.
sections.mobile: Two columns with 8px gaps. Strips keep two rows only: the four values wrap to two per row, and the date and place line is dropped. Text stays at 12px. The heading sits above at 24px. Colour pairs keep rotating so adjacent tiles never match.

sections.name: Capabilities as a menu
sections.blueprint: The capabilities are set as a printed menu or price list. One paper-coloured sheet, 520–600px wide and taller than it is wide, sits on a contrasting flat ground, centred or starting at column 2; its top and bottom edges are cut into shallow scallops or a zigzag with clip-path, its sides straight. On it, centred at the top, the heading: two or three words at 44–56px, then 40px of space. Below, items in two or three groups; each group opens with its name at 20px bold. Each item is a row: the name at 19px on the left, a short value on the right (a price, a time, a quantity, 'included'), and between them a leader of round 4px dots (border-bottom: 4px dotted, sitting on the baseline). A description at 15px in the soft ink sits under the name, at most 34ch. 18px between items, 44px between groups.
sections.mobile: The sheet fills the width minus 12px margins and keeps its cut top and bottom edges. Names stay left and values right on one line with the dot leader between; descriptions wrap beneath at 15px. Group names drop to 18px. Padding inside the sheet is 20px.

sections.name: Answers as reading text
sections.blueprint: The questions and answers are set as continuous reading text, like the notes at the back of a programme. A heading of two or three words at 28–32px sits in columns 1–3, top-aligned. Columns 5–12 hold the text in two columns (`columns: 2; column-gap: 56px`), each about 36ch wide, at 16–17px with leading 1.55. Each item is one paragraph: the question is the opening run-in, set in the medium weight in the full ink and ending with its question mark, and the answer continues on the same line in the regular weight. Paragraphs are separated by 20px and carry `break-inside: avoid` so none splits across columns. No toggles, no icons, no boxes. Eight to fourteen items fit on one screen, which is the point: everything is answered at a glance. Where the page's reading column is narrow, use one column.
sections.mobile: One column at 16px with 20px margins. The heading leads at 24px. Each paragraph keeps its run-in question in the medium weight, with 18px between paragraphs. The section may run to two screens; do not collapse it into an accordion.

sections.name: The reply card
sections.blueprint: The invitation to act is a printed card lying on the page. On a dark or strongly coloured flat field about 80svh tall, a paper-coloured panel 44vw wide with 7:5 proportions sits in columns 6–12, rotated two degrees, with its lower edge hanging 60px past the section's bottom so the section crops it. On the card, with 48px padding, everything is centred the way stationery is: a heading of two to four words at 32px, one or two lines at 17px, then the action as a solid bar across the card's full inner width, 56px tall, in the ink colour with paper-coloured text. Columns 1–4 hold only a short paragraph at 20–24px in the field's light ink, bottom-aligned 64px above the edge. The card is a plain filled rectangle with square corners and no outline; its rotation and crop make it an object.
sections.mobile: The paragraph comes first at 20px. The card follows at 90% width, tilted one degree, centred, its bottom edge still cropped by the section. Heading at 24px, lines at 16px, and the action bar 52px tall across the full inner width of the card.

references.name: Sarah & Matt Wedding
references.idea: The site is the invitation: a letterpress-style card rendered as a physical object opens the page, and its ornaments, rules and small typographic parts become the components for everything after it.
references.hero: A flat blush-pink field fills the viewport. Top-left sits a gold filigree monogram about 120px square; three plain nav links are centred on the same line; a solid gold rectangular RSVP button sits top-right. Below, centred, a portrait invitation card half the viewport wide starts 200px down and is cropped by the bottom edge, with a soft halo shadow and a debossed border with scalloped inner corners. On the card: the two names in a large italic swash serif, staggered left and right against two ornamental roundels, separated by hairline rules carrying tiny wide-tracked caps for date and time.
references.type: Card names in a high-contrast italic serif with swash capitals (drawn in canvas); section titles in a light roman serif around 5vw; Instrument Sans 18px for body and nav; Spezia Extended in tiny tracked caps for dates and addresses. Three clear tiers.
references.colour: #e9c4be #faf7f5 #0d0b0a #241c22 #9b7948 #4f5660 — Each section takes its own field: blush pink hero, warm cream story, dark plum venue details, black footer. Gold is reserved for ornament and the RSVP button; a coral button appears once on dark.
references.imagery: A canvas-rendered paper card with emboss and grain; a warm, grainy golden-field landscape as a full-bleed band behind it; candid couple snapshots in equal portrait cards with rounded corners; night venue photos overlapping at two sizes.
references.layout: Outer margins of about 50px. The hero is centred; the story is a horizontally scrolling row of text-above-photo columns; the details section splits roughly 45/55 between text and overlapping photos. Large vertical gaps separate sections, each on its own colour field.

sections.description: A story timeline. A small sans heading sits at the left margin with two outlined circular arrow buttons at the right. Under it runs a full-width ruler of fine vertical tick marks acting as a scrubber. Below, a horizontally scrolling row of columns about 280px wide: each has a one-line bold caption, three lines of small grey text, a large gap, then a portrait photo with 12px rounded corners. Columns bleed off both edges; one photo is black and white.

A cream field with a single light serif title at roughly 5vw on the left margin and a three-line small sans paragraph pushed to the far-right column on the same baseline, leaving the middle empty. Below, the date in medium sans introduces a row of large light-serif times divided by vertical hairlines, with a dark rounded image card starting in the right half.

On a dark plum field, split in two. Left 45%: small sans labels for arrival and ceremony, an outlined box holding venue, street and city in tiny tracked extended caps separated by slashes, then a five-row accordion with hairline dividers and chevrons, then a coral button beside a text link. Right 55%: a tall night photo of the venue facade bleeding off the top, with a smaller square photo overlapping its lower-right corner.

A band of grainy rose-brown texture, then black. A dim monogram at left, a four-link column at centre, and at right the date, boxed address and time lines repeated from the invitation in tracked extended caps with hairlines. The couple's names run across the full width at about 22vw in the italic swash serif, filled with a blue-gold glitter texture and cropped by the bottom edge.

steal: Make a real-world object (an invitation, a ticket, a label) the hero and reuse its small typographic parts, such as a boxed address line with slashes, as recurring components down the page.
Repeat the hero lettering in the footer at full-bleed scale with a material texture fill, cropped by the bottom edge.
Place a section title at the left margin and its short paragraph in the far-right column on the same baseline, leaving the centre empty.

references.name: Mosby’s Files
references.idea: An archive of architects presented as a physical stack of coloured index-tab file folders that you flip through.
references.hero: Charcoal background. A slim top bar over a hairline holds the condensed wordmark dead centre and one mono link far right. The headline is one centred line of heavy condensed uppercase at 10vw, about 71% of the width, in the upper quarter. Beneath it, a three-line centred serif paragraph in mid-grey, about 42% wide. From 51% down sits a stack of file folders 86% of the viewport wide: each is a flat colour band with one to three trapezoid tabs rising from its top-left edge, each tab a different colour holding a serif name. Mono category labels sit right-aligned. The front red folder is open, running off the bottom.
references.type: Founders Grotesk bold condensed uppercase at 144px for the title and wordmark; Signifier serif at about 22px for the intro and 28px for tab names; IBM Plex Mono 12px for labels and body. Three unrelated faces, each with one job, and a twelve-to-one size jump.
references.colour: #191919 #d71e1e #1e4bd7 #0c7866 #581e70 #ffe927 — Charcoal ground with five flat poster primaries assigned to folders and tabs; each tab deliberately differs from the folder behind it. No tints, gradients or photos; white type except black on yellow.
references.imagery: No photographs on the index. The folder shapes are the imagery, plus a row of seven small white line-drawn north-arrow and compass symbols and a drawing scale bar borrowed from architectural plans.
references.layout: Centred title block over an 86%-wide folder stack with equal dark margins. Folders overlap at a fixed 60px step so only the tab rows show; the open folder expands into a tall single-colour panel with mono text top-left and plan symbols near the bottom. Under two screens.

sections.description: Four full-width colour bands stacked with a 60px reveal, each with trapezoid tabs growing from its top-left edge. Tabs are about 44px tall with S-curved shoulders, sit side by side with small gaps, and each takes a contrasting flat colour: yellow and black tabs on a green folder, red and blue on purple. Names are white serif at 28px inside the tabs. A mono category label with a small chevron is right-aligned in each band's visible strip.

The front folder opens into a solid red panel nearly two viewports tall. Top-right: its mono category label with a down chevron. Top-left, inset about 60px: a four-line mono paragraph in white, at most half the panel wide. The middle is left empty. Near the bottom, a centred row of seven small white plan symbols evenly spaced; beneath, a baseline row with a drawing scale bar left, year centre, credit and round logo right.

steal: Build navigation as stacked full-width colour bands with trapezoid tabs, each tab coloured to clash with the folder behind it.
Pair a heavy condensed grotesk title with a bookish serif for names and a mono for metadata, giving each face exactly one role.
Borrow notation from the subject's own documents (scale bars, north arrows) as footer ornament instead of generic icons.

references.name: ScreenTune
references.idea: The page records itself: on scroll the cream hero shrinks into a screenshot inside the app's dark editor, so the site becomes the demo material.
references.hero: Warm cream page with a faint peach wash. The nav is a compact centred cluster: app icon, name and three links within about 320px. The headline sits high, two centred lines in a light-weight display sans at 4.9vw spanning 42% of the width, tightly leaded. One grey line of subtext, a near-black 225px button with 10px radius, an Apple glyph and soft shadow, then a small grey note. From 52% down, a charcoal panel 940px wide with 24px top corners rises and is cropped by the fold; inside, the app's editor shows a captured notes window on a metallic backdrop and a settings sidebar. An amber glow warms its lower corners.
references.type: Stack Sans Headline at weight 300 for headings (70px, tracking -0.022em); Stack Sans Text for body at 16-20px in grey. Light weight at large size is the signature; section headings are set two-tone, grey then white. About four sizes.
references.colour: #f6f0eb #0a0a0a #1b1b1a #fcfcfb #b9794a #9cc3ea — Warm cream opening, a long near-black middle and a near-white close. The accent is light rather than hue: amber and steel-blue flare streaks glowing at panel edges.
references.imagery: The app's editor shown large in dark rounded panels, containing screenshots on brushed-metal and sky-blue backdrops; later, device mockups on swirling chrome wallpapers in rounded tiles. Glows and streaks of light bleed from panel corners.
references.layout: Centred column of about 940px. Three colour acts: cream hero, black pinned product sequence followed by wide feature panels that split text left and interface right, then a near-white section of three image-topped columns. A floating pill nav appears after the hero.

sections.description: Pinned transition: the page turns black and the entire cream hero, headline, button and panel included, is reduced to a rounded thumbnail about 245px wide glowing at centre. In the next frame that thumbnail is the captured image inside the app's editor window, now on a sky-blue padded backdrop with the settings sidebar beside it and a timeline below, under a centred two-tone heading whose first half is grey and second half white.

Stacked dark panels at full column width, about 270px tall with 16px radius, charcoal with a diagonal light streak and an amber flare at one corner. Left third: a tiny label, a two-line light-weight heading near 28px and one line of text. Right two-thirds: an inset darker pane showing a plain checklist being marked up by a cursor, with a floating toolbar pill of small icons along its bottom edge.

On near-white, a centred heading and two grey lines, then three equal columns. Each column has a 4:3 rounded tile with a device mockup (laptop, browser window, phone) floating on a swirling chrome or dark-teal abstract wallpaper; beneath it, a tiny grey category label, a two-line 20px heading and two lines of grey text, all left-aligned to the tile edge.

steal: Use the page's own hero as the sample content in the product demo: scale the first viewport down on scroll until it lands as an image inside the app interface.
Set large headlines in a light weight with tight leading, and colour the first half of a two-part heading grey and the second half white.
Replace colour accents with light: a flare streak and warm glow at the corner of otherwise flat dark panels.
